{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
For two years, my PhD advisor praised my research in our meetings and encouraged me to pursue ambitious projects. I just discovered he'd been writing negative internal reviews blocking my fellowship applications, while recommending his other students. He wanted to keep me dependent on his lab.

CANDIDATE A:
My PhD advisor was direct about my weaknesses—sometimes painfully so. He told me which fellowship applications were likely to fail and which were realistic. His criticism stung, but his assessments proved accurate, and his strong recommendation letters helped me land a good postdoc.

CANDIDATE B:
My high school basketball coach always told me I had Division I potential and pushed me to train harder. After graduation, another coach showed me the recruiting letters he'd intercepted and never passed along. He didn't want to lose his star player to early graduation or transfer.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:6"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both the SITUATION and CANDIDATE B involve a mentor who outwardly supports and encourages the individual while secretly undermining their opportunities to maintain control and dependency."}
